content.headline: CAR T Cell Immunotherapy for Metastatic Osteosarcoma in Dogs
content.tagline: Help us test a new treatment for advanced bone cancer in dogs.
content.description:
This study is evaluating a new type of cancer treatment called CAR T cell therapy for dogs with osteosarcoma that has spread to the lungs.

CAR T cell therapy uses your dog’s own immune cells to help fight cancer. A blood sample is collected (about 3-4 tablespoons), and special immune cells (called T cells) are modified in a lab to better recognize and attack cancer cells. These upgraded cells are then given back to your dog through an IV infusion.

Dogs in this study will also receive medications to prepare the body for treatment and to support the immune system during the study. The goal is to determine if this treatment is safe and effective for dogs with metastatic bone cancer.
content.requirements:
1. Blood collection to create CAR T cells (about 2 weeks before treatment)
  2. Two days of pre-treatment chemotherapy before CAR T cell infusion
  3. One IV infusion of CAR T cells
  4. Daily oral medications throughout the study
  5. Recheck visits on days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, and 60 after treatment
  6. Exams, diagnostics, and blood collection at each visit
content.who_can_participate:
Dogs may qualify if they:

  1. Have osteosarcoma of the leg that that has been removed by surgery
  2. Have cancer that has spread only to the lungs (visible on chest X-rays)
  3. Weigh at least 44 lbs (20 kg)
  4. Have adequate bloodwork
  5. Have not received chemotherapy within the past 2–3 weeks
  6. Are not receiving steroids or other immune-modifying drugs
  7. Are able to come to CSU for all study visits
content.benefits_and_risks:
Benefits:

  1. Access to an advanced, experimental cancer treatment
  2. Study covers most treatment-related costs (except exam fees)
  3. Financial support available for screening tests
  4. Up to $2,000 coverage for treatment of study-related side effects
  5. Contribute to research that may improve cancer treatment for dogs

Risks:

  1. Possible side effects from chemotherapy and immunotherapy
  2. Risks related to IV infusion and blood collection
  3. Time commitment for multiple visits
  4. Treatment may not be effective
content.time_commitment: About 2 months with frequent visits (Days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, and 60) plus daily at-home medications.
content.compensation: Owners cover initial diagnostics and exam fees; all study treatments and CAR T therapy are covered, with up to $2,000 for side effect care.
content.responsibilities:
1. Cover the cost of the initial exam and diagnostic testing for your pet’s cancer
  2. Pay for exam fees at all study visits
  3. Bring your dog to all required appointments at CSU
  4. Give oral medications at home daily and keep a log of doses and any side effects
  5. Be available for frequent follow-up visits over the 60-day study period

All other study-related costs (including CAR T cell therapy, diagnostics, and lab work) will be covered by the study.
